presentation.beta_note: Beta version - the analysis and the welding tests are still being checked.
presentation.description_avant: A tool that helps you prepare a WPS (welding procedure specification). It calculates the chromium and nickel equivalents, places the joint on the
presentation.description_apres: , estimates the preheat, the t8/5 cooling time and the expected hardness, then compares the results with the limits given by the standards. The tool switches between carbon steel, stainless steel and dissimilar joints on its own. It does not replace a WPQR or a workshop test.

normes.objet: WPS - content of the welding procedure specification
Arc welding - general rules, thermal efficiency factors
Ferritic steels - preheat and t8/5 cooling time
Steels for sour service (H2S) - hardness limit

onglets.description: You enter the base metals, the process and the joint. The tool runs the analysis, ranks the 7 most robust filler metals and gives the summary on the same page.
Reference steel grades and filler metals, with free entry for a grade that is not in the list.
Updates to the tool, and contact for any question, idea or proposal to work together.

annonces.intro: The weldability calculator is still being developed. New features are added step by step, update after update.
annonces.a_venir: The next steps are the calculation of the cooling time, to avoid metallurgical risks, and more grades in the base metal and filler metal databases.
annonces.beta_avant: The tool is in beta. The
annonces.beta_apres: is being tested by several users, and tests on different materials and processes are planned to check how reliable it is.

banque.note_indicative: Typical compositions (middle of the range given by the standard, or a typical supplier value). They do not give the composition of a real heat. Use the material certificate (3.1 or 3.2) for a qualified file.
banque.apport_vide: No filler metal listed for this process.

parametres.intro: Enter the metals, the process and the joint. The tool proposes the electrical settings, and you can change them in custom mode.
parametres.apport_note: The list is filtered by process. For a grade that is not listed, add a manual composition.
parametres.apport_vide: No filler metal listed for this process - use free entry
parametres.apport_analyse_note: The filler metal is proposed further down, in the analysis, after a calculation over the whole dilution range of the process.
parametres.apport_enrobage_note: Filtering by covering type still to be completed in the database.
parametres.mode_auto: AUTO: values proposed by the tool
parametres.mode_personnalise: CUSTOM: I enter my own values
parametres.mode_aide: You can impose your own settings: choose CUSTOM in the list above, then change the current, the voltage, the travel speed or the heat input.
parametres.tungstene_conseil: Preselected: {designation}, suitable for {intensite} A in DCEN. The type and the diameter change how the arc behaves, but they do not change the heat input calculation.
parametres.tungstene_indisponible: No electrode in the database covers this current.
parametres.comp_manuelle_titre: Composition used for the calculation (you can edit it)
parametres.vitesse_note: Typical value filled in for the process. You can adjust it.
parametres.reglages_note: In custom mode, changing the current, the voltage or the travel speed recalculates the heat input. Changing the heat input recalculates the travel speed, without touching the current or the voltage.
parametres.enrobage_non_couvert: BWRA is not available for this covering type: the Seferian result is shown, without treating the covering as rutile.
parametres.note_tig_hetero: Reduced current - protects the stainless steel side.
parametres.dilution_note: The weld metal mixes three parts: melted metal A, melted metal B and filler metal. The three parts add up to 100 %. Dilution is the sum of the two melted base metal parts.
parametres.dilution_erreur: The three parts must add up to 100 %.
parametres.dilution_indicative_note: Typical value for the process and the edge preparation. A real figure needs a macro-examination of the actual joint.
parametres.resultats_note: Q = k × En, where k is the thermal efficiency factor of the process (EN 1011-1). Values in kJ/cm.

analyse.intro: The joint is placed on the Schaeffler diagram and 7 filler metals are compared over the whole dilution range of the process. The tool calculates and proposes; it does not qualify.
analyse.intro_carbone: Cold cracking risk for this joint between non-alloy or low-alloy steels: carbon equivalent and the right preheat method (Seferian or BWRA). The tool calculates and proposes; it does not qualify.
analyse.message_vide: Enter metals A and B above (composition) to display the Schaeffler diagram and the filler metal selection.
analyse.heterogene_note: Dissimilar joint: the analysis stays focused on the weld metal and the Schaeffler diagram. Preheat is not calculated in this case.
analyse.carbone_message: The Schaeffler diagram does not apply to non-alloy or low-alloy steels. For this joint, the useful analysis is the cold cracking risk, estimated below with the carbon equivalent and the most suitable preheat method.
analyse.carbone_seuil: Guide value: weldable without preheat if CE_IIW < 0.42 %.
analyse.methode_seferian_msg: Seferian method used: the process or the covering family is not in the BWRA table available.
analyse.methode_bwra_msg: BWRA method used: covered electrode process with the hydrogen class of the consumable filled in.
analyse.joint_centre_plage: Representative joint: middle of the range, at {valeur} % dilution
analyse.diagramme_intro_court: An interactive reading of the Schaeffler diagram: the tool calculates the dilution, places the joint and ranks the filler metals. The results stay metallurgical estimates.
analyse.diagramme_difference_titre: Why is this diagram different from the one in textbooks?
analyse.diagramme_difference_intro: The Soudabilite.com chart follows the principles of the original Schaeffler diagram and turns them into an interactive decision aid.
analyse.diagramme_difference_calcul_titre: A calculation made for your joint
analyse.diagramme_difference_calcul_texte: The tool places metal A, metal B, their dilution, the filler metal and the estimated final composition of the joint. You see straight away how the mixture changes the expected structure.
analyse.diagramme_difference_traces_texte: The original boundaries have been digitised and some intermediate lines come from interpolation. They may look slightly different from printed copies or course material, but the chromium and nickel equivalents used to place the joint are unchanged.
analyse.diagramme_difference_lecture_texte: The blue zone is the first target of the tool. The green zone widens the range to look at. The white corridor keeps a historical fallback when the first two zones cannot be reached.
analyse.diagramme_difference_limite_texte: The diagram estimates a metallurgical trend from the compositions and the dilution you entered. It does not guarantee the real structure of the weld metal or the properties of the joint. The final check is the WPS, the WPQR that applies and, when needed, a real ferrite measurement.
analyse.apports_note: Each filler metal is checked over the whole dilution range of the process. The ranking looks first at the worst result found, then at the share of the range inside the ideal zone. Click a row to see the detail on the diagram.
analyse.apports_vide: No filler metal listed for this process - use manual entry.
analyse.duplex_indisponible: The duplex and super duplex branch is still being checked. No filler metal selection is proposed yet for these base metals.
analyse.plage_explication: The result is based on the least favourable point of the whole process range.
analyse.plage_en_zone_ideale: of the range in the ideal zone
analyse.apport_manuel_nom: Name of the proposed filler metal
analyse.apport_manuel_note: A manual filler metal is calculated and ranked with the same rules as the database. Its real rank is shown even if it is outside the top 7.
analyse.ferrite_note: The ferrite content is estimated by interpolation between the iso-ferrite lines of the Schaeffler diagram. Duplex grades are outside the current scope.
analyse.ferrite_hors_domaine: Ferrite not estimated outside the iso-line area
analyse.risque_austenite: hot cracking risk found outside the accepted zones
analyse.risque_martensite: cold cracking risk found in the martensitic zone
analyse.synth_choisir: Select a filler metal in the table to see the result for the joint.
analyse.aide_dilution: No filler metal stays in an accepted zone over the whole process range. Narrow the range only if you have a measurement or reliable workshop feedback.

zones_explication.texte: Austenite is usually a ductile structure, mainly promoted by nickel. If the weld metal becomes almost fully austenitic, the hot cracking risk rises during solidification. A small amount of ferrite usually helps to limit this risk.

Martensite can appear when some steels cool down too fast. It is hard but brittle. With welding stresses and hydrogen, it raises the cold cracking risk. Preheating and low hydrogen practice reduce this risk.
Ferrite is a structure mainly promoted by chromium. Too much ferrite can lower the toughness and the ductility of the joint, especially after exposure to a high temperature.
This zone holds austenite and martensite. The martensite makes the joint more sensitive to cold cracking, above all when the joint is heavily restrained or when hydrogen is not controlled.

This zone combines the possible brittleness of martensite with the limits of a high ferrite content. It is usually unfavourable and calls for a careful check of the filler metal, the cooling and the welding conditions.

zones_explication.titre: Zone A+M+F: austenite, martensite and ferrite
zones_explication.texte: The grey zone holds the three structures: austenite, martensite and ferrite. The white S-shaped corridor lies inside this zone. It is a fallback solution, accepted after the ideal zone and the acceptable zone.

This zone combines austenite and ferrite. It is often the target for welding stainless steels and some dissimilar joints, because the right balance limits the hot cracking risk without giving too much ferrite.

mecanismes.texte: It appears while the weld metal solidifies. Shrinkage stresses, some impurities and a fully austenitic structure all make it more likely. A suitable amount of delta ferrite helps to lower this risk.

It can appear several hours after welding. It usually comes from a brittle structure, residual stresses and diffusible hydrogen together. Preheating, controlled cooling and low hydrogen consumables reduce this risk.

analyse.etagement_titre: Order of priority of the zones
analyse.etagement_intro: How to read the diagram and the ranking:

etagement.texte: The first target of the tool, between 5 and 15 % delta ferrite. The ranking favours the middle of this band, where the balance between hot cracking and mechanical properties is usually the best.

A wider range, from 0 to 20 % ferrite. The result can still be used, but it must be looked at with more care: too little ferrite favours hot cracking, while a high ferrite content can lower some properties of the joint.
This S-shaped corridor lies inside the grey A+M+F zone. A result here is accepted as a fallback, after the blue ideal zone and the green acceptable zone.

analyse.diag_corridor_titre: A+M+F safety corridor - accepted after the ideal zone and then the acceptable zone.
analyse.diag_axe_x: % Cr eq = Cr + Mo + 1.5 Si + 0.5 Nb
analyse.diag_mur_sigma: Cr eq = 25: sigma phase limit - above it, brittle intermetallic precipitation
